name: Solaris
description: A star 50 parsecs away, 87% of the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 104780: radius 0.868 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 0.364 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.053) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 104780: effective temperature 4814 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.059)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 104780: distance 49.743 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.012), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 50 parsecs away, 87% of the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 0.364 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,814 K, so 0.868 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 104780: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: BD+14 4559
quotes.card: BD+14 4559 is a star with an exoplanetary companion in the northern constellation of Pegasus.
quotes.introduction: During the 2019 NameExoWorlds campaign, the star was named Solaris by Poland after a 1961 science fiction novel about an ocean-covered exoplanet by Polish writer Stanisław Lem.
